passages.title: Reading Text
paragraphs: What’s Our Next Direction in Life?[1] It is a matter of fact that the future is full of uncertainties. We are overwhelmed by the exciting adventures ahead of us. However, the mere thought of planning for our future at different times of our lives, from pursuing higher education, finding employment to maintaining interpersonal relationships and taking on marital and family roles, could just be intimidating. We are constantly bothered by the anxiety of not knowing about our next direction. It is worthwhile to think about what we wish to achieve at different stages of our lives, but this is a hard question to answer.[2] As we advance through different levels of the education system, it appears that everything has been well-planned. We move on to the next level of the education upon the end of an academic year. We are “spoon-fed” with knowledge and always told exactly what we are expected to do and learn. We are accustomed to following instructions and walking the path laid out in front of us. In the face of adversity and problems, there are always people, such as teachers and parents, to offer help and smooth out the obstacles. However, things don’t happen this way as we progress to the next stage and enter the workforce.[3] Many university graduates find themselves feeling insecure or frustrated. Job seekers, especially those who have left the schooling system early, need to face a lot of challenges in pursuing their ideal career. Penny Ma, a recent graduate holding a bachelor’s degree in commerce from the Island University, said, “I’m so happy that I finally graduated from university, but I really don’t know what I’m going to do next.” Those who are studying for a career with better prospects may think more optimistically. There exists a small community of incredibly daring fresh graduates, such as John Li, who has just completed a higher diploma in fashion design and would like to start a business with his friends. “It would be fascinating to have our own brand of clothing and fashionable products,” the fresh graduate expressed enthusiastically. [4] People may end up doing different jobs across a variety of sectors, such as retailing, transport, journalism, accounting, clerical work, and performing arts, to name a few. No matter which field we are in, it is important to know what we want to gain from our jobs – be it high salary, job satisfaction, professional status, promotion prospects, opportunities for travelling and working overseas. We have to be aware that in addition to having the right personality, relevant education background, professional qualifications, work experience, as well as knowledge and skills are needed if we desire to take up certain jobs or positions.[5] Victoria Mak, the career advisor at Peninsula College, has some advice for students who have difficulty coming up with their future plans or feel anxious about making career choices. “Start by exploring your personal interests and get some relevant experience, say through volunteering, in the fields you are interested in. You never know where it will lead you, but if you’re committed to spending your time doing what interests you, that’s a life well lived,” said Ms Mak. David Lynn, a career coach in a leading recruitment agency, suggests that students should, since a year before graduation, set aside a little time every month to explore relevant websites, visit career shows and job fairs, or talk to professionals of their personal network about their jobs to keep up with the current job market. [6] For graduates or school leavers who wish to set up their own businesses, some successful entrepreneurs have shared some valuable tips. Brian Chen, founder of Excellence Co. reminds beginners of the importance of lifelong learning – “Work hard towards your goal, even just a small step at a time. Never be complacent and keep learning throughout your life. In my 50s, I’m still refreshing myself every day to keep abreast of the times.” Jason Chu, the CEO of GroupBuy, believes that it is important for young people to examine if they have the essential qualities and personality traits to manage a company of their own before starting a business. “In addition to being innovative and sensitive to the market needs, an entrepreneur should be highly motivated, adaptive and resilient,” he explained. He advises young people to develop their business idea more fully and do a reality check before investing money, resources and time. “Haste makes waste – calculate the cost and risk, talk to experienced people in the field about your business plan and shadow similar businesses to test the waters first,” the veteran added. [7] One positive note that young school leavers should always bear in mind is that no career choice is final. There is no such thing as a dream or ideal job, and if there really is, it comes through a process of trial and error. Research has shown that graduates usually have four to five jobs before they really find the right profession and work their way up. Therefore, there is no need to worry about making a wrong choice that you have to live with forever. A young person’s first choice will rarely be their last. Many people even switch their tracks and develop a second career later on, with the connections they have established, as well as the transferrable skills and experiences they have acquired from their previous jobs. Graduates should, therefore, be more open about the first job and allow themselves more time to explore different career options. [8] Needless to say, life is an ongoing learning journey with many unpredictable challenges. Yet, there are also endless possibilities. After acquiring fundamental knowledge and skills through formal education, we have to make use of what we have learnt to seek employment and opportunities for success in our chosen fields of endeavour. Whichever path we take, it is essential to keep learning on the job to equip ourselves for career advancement. Lifelong learning is perhaps the only key to success in the world of changes and uncertainties. Despite a lot of uneasy feelings, it’s time to summon up our courage to embrace the unknown and eagerly await the wonderful adventures in the future.
